sources_considered.why: Nature news feature, 21 January 2025, on the state of hallucination research. Headline and standfirst are readable; the body is paywalled.
Georgia Tech summary of the Nature feature, with the line saying researchers are working to make hallucinations less frequent.
OpenAI system card for o3-mini (launched end of January 2025) with measured hallucination rates and OpenAI's own caveat.
September 2024 preprint arguing hallucinations cannot be eliminated. Outside the target period, so context only.
2024 Nature paper on semantic entropy: a statistics-grounded method that detects only a subset of hallucinations. Possible counterpoint; context only.
I could not find a January 2025 snapshot of the leaderboard.

evidence_items.locator: standfirst, under headline 'AI hallucinations can't be stopped — but these techniques can limit their damage'

receipt.public_excerpt: Developers have tricks to stop artificial intelligence from making things up, but large language models are still struggling to tell the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

evidence_items.explanation: A major science journal's survey of the field in January 2025 says hallucinations can't be stopped and that existing techniques only limit the damage. That matches 'no principled trustworthy answer'.

evidence_items.locator: section 4.1.3 Hallucination Evaluations, Table 3 (PersonQA hallucination rate: 52.4% GPT-4o-mini, 27.4% o1-mini, 14.8% o3-mini)

receipt.public_excerpt:
More work is needed to understand hallucinations holistically, particularly in domains not covered
by our evaluations (e.g., chemistry).

evidence_items.explanation: OpenAI's newest model at the end of January 2025 still hallucinated on 14.8% of PersonQA questions, and OpenAI said more work was needed to understand hallucinations. No general solution was in hand.

evidence_items.publisher: Georgia Institute of Technology, College of Computing

receipt.public_excerpt: Vempala and others are working on ways to make hallucinations less frequent and less problematic.

evidence_items.explanation: Summary of the Nature feature. It shows that researchers' goal in January 2025 was to reduce hallucinations, not that they had solved them.

receipt.public_excerpt: Here we develop new methods grounded in statistics, proposing entropy-based uncertainty estimators for LLMs to detect a subset of hallucinations—confabulations—which are arbitrary and incorrect generations.

evidence_items.explanation: The strongest counterpoint I found: a principled, theory-grounded method from 2024. But it only detects a subset of hallucinations and does not prevent them, so it is not a full trustworthy answer.

unresolved_gaps: The body of the Nature feature is paywalled; only its headline, standfirst and a university summary could be read.
